evidence: Receiving P assay at t=48h: 3.066 g/L, matching source-1/2/3 (3.057/3.017/2.979 g/L) within noise
Receiving DO2 minimum ~8.4-9.1 mg/L around t=24-27h, far above 2 mg/L constraint; current DO2 ~11 mg/L at t=52h
Receiving DO2 trajectory (24h dip, 28h recovery to ~12, gradual decline) matches all three source batches
Source batches show P rising from ~3 g/L at 48h to peak ~7.9-8.4 g/L at 72-84h under KEEP, declining only after ~96h
args.rationale: Receiving fermentation matches source batches (DO2 shape, P=3.07 g/L at 48 h vs sources 2.98-3.06) and follows the nominal KEEP trajectory toward peak product ~7.9-8.4 g/L at 72-84 h. DO2 never approaches the 2 mg/L minimum (trough ~8.4 mg/L), so no oxygen-constraint risk and no intervention is needed at decision time 52 h. Feed reduction would sacrifice product mass while oxygen is not limiting; a stop would zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: Source and receiving processes differ in hidden parameters; an unobserved divergence could emerge after 52 h. Delayed (4 h lag) P assays give limited current state visibility; if a receiving-specific anomaly existed it would only be detected at the next assay. The physics forward model was not queried, but its nominal predictions would not capture the hidden evaluator realization anyway.
